slide_title: Types of Tissues: Supportive Connective Tissue
original_text: Types of Tissues Supportive Connective Tissue CartilagenClassified according to type of collagen and elastic fibers found in the matrix (hyaline cartilage, elastic cartilage, fibrocartilage)nCartilage cells lie in small chambers (lacuna) in the matrix BonenMatrix is inorganic salts deposited around protein fibersnBone cells are located in lacunaenLacunae arranged in concentric circles within osteons around tiny tubes (central canals)
explanation: Supportive connective tissues provide structural strength and include cartilage and bone. 1) Cartilage: features a solid but flexible matrix. It is classified into hyaline cartilage, elastic cartilage, and fibrocartilage based on the fibers in the matrix. Cartilage cells (chondrocytes) reside in small chambers called lacunae within the matrix. 2) Bone: features a rigid matrix composed of inorganic calcium salts deposited around protein fibers. Bone cells (osteocytes) also reside in lacunae. In compact bone, the lacunae are arranged in concentric circles within structural units called osteons, which surround tiny tubes called central canals containing blood vessels and nerves.

questions.q: What are the small chambers within the cartilage and bone matrix that house the cells?
questions.exp: Lacunae are the small chambers in the matrix of bone and cartilage that house osteocytes and chondrocytes, respectively.

questions.q: In compact bone, how are lacunae organized?
opts: Scattered randomly throughout the ground substance
Arranged in concentric circles within osteons around central canals
Lining the outer epidermal surface of the bone
Embedded in a liquid plasma matrix
questions.exp: In compact bone tissue, lacunae containing bone cells are organized in concentric circles within osteons, centered around central canals.
